To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MSI causes a conspicuous oedematous swelling of glia and neuronal cells in tissue culture, and that this effect occurs most intensely in oligodendrocytes.

MSI in a high concentration of 10 ^{−3} M caused, shortly after administration, conspicuous oedema in the perikaryon and the processes of astrocyte cells and in oligodendrocyte perikarya, which were accompanied by the fragmentation and destruction of the processes and the contraction of the perikarya.
MSI causes, at a concentration of 1 mM, a swelling of glial and neuronal cells in brain and cerebellar tissue cultures, which is followed by a retraction and destruction of the cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of methioninesulphoximino on the behaviour of glia cells and nerve cells in vitro.
the effect of methioninesulphoximide on the behaviour of glial and neuronal cells in tissue culture.
the effects of methionine sulphoximine (M.S.I.) on the morphology of the glial and neuronal cells in tissue culture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MSI is a toxic agent which acts on glia elements in a very specific manner and causes a swelling which in the course of time leads to a disintegration of the cells.
MSI causes a swelling of glial cells, which is accompanied by a shrinkage of the cell body and fragmentation of the processes.

in a concentration of MSI of 3 M, a considerable swelling of the glia cells is observed, which is accompanied by an increase in the frequency of movements of cytoplasmic structures, by a decrease of their velocity and finally by a destruction of glial elements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of MSI on brain and cerebellar explants is a toxic one, and that the most susceptible cell type is the oligodendrogia.

MSI in a high concentration (10−3 M) causes a conspicuous swelling of all cellular elements, which is accompanied by an increased motility of the cytoplasmic organelles, a fragmentation and destruction of the processes of the oligodendra and astrocytes, and a retraction and fragmentation of the neuronal processes.
the effect of MSI in a concentration 10−3 is to cause an oedema of glial elements and a destruction of the oligodentroglia, while neurons are less affected.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of MSI on glia is more pronounced than that on neurons.
the use of the MSI in concentrations higher than 10−5M is not recommended for the culture of brain explants, as the glial elements are damaged and the growth of the explants inhibited.
MSI causes a swelling of glial cells, especially of the oligodenedroglia, and a shrinkage and destruction of the neuronal elements.
